name: verified-monitoring
narrative: David opens the independent survey's dashboard — the six-round trend. It confirms a big rise in vitamin-A coverage, but below what his program reports. On the map, service delivery points fill only the intervention ward; the survey covered both. He toggles layers — service delivery, survey, the plan's sampled PSUs — showing where each looked. David checks the surveyors, one row each. The Connect app requires you to be within 15 meters to submit a survey, so everyone is 100% compliant. He reads the rest — photos, on-primary rate, back-checks. One's flagged. David opens that surveyor's back-check: an independent enumerator re-visited the same households. Original vs re-survey — sex, age, roof, location, vitamin-A result. Finally the Distributions table: the flagged surveyor's interviews ran impossibly fast, their roof-type answers collapse onto one value — two more flags. Everyone else varies normally.

david.name: David Mensah
david.intro: David manages a Connect program delivering vitamin-A home visits. His frontline workers log every visit through Connect and the coverage figure looks good — but David wants independent, drillable proof his program is actually reaching households and changing outcomes, not merely that visits were logged. He wants to see the verification machinery itself: the survey's own per-surveyor quality and a back-check David can read row by row, including whether any one surveyor's data can be trusted.

slides.title: The goal — independent, drillable proof the program works
slides.narration: David's program looks good on paper — his workers log every vitamin-A visit, and the coverage number is high. But a logged visit isn't proof a household was reached, or that outcomes changed. So he commissioned an independent survey — and he wants to see the verification machinery itself: the trend round over round, each surveyor's quality, and a back-check he can read row by row. Not 'trust us' — proof he can drill into.

slides.title: Six bi-monthly rounds over time — the gap holds
slides.narration: David opens the independent survey's six-round trend. It confirms a real rise in vitamin-A coverage — but below what his programme reports.

slides.title: Where delivery happened vs where the survey checked (the map moves)
slides.narration: On the map, delivery points fill only the intervention ward; the survey checked both. So the gap is real, not a coverage artifact.

slides.title: The per-surveyor quality scorecard catches a surveyor
slides.narration: He checks the surveyors, one row each. One — T6 — is flagged: its quality scores trip the review threshold.

slides.title: The independent back-check confirms it
slides.narration: He opens T6's back-check: an independent enumerator re-visited the households, and the answers don't match.

slides.title: GPS is clean — the Distributions screen catches the fabrication
slides.narration: And the Distributions screen — T6's interviews ran impossibly fast and too uniform: statistical fingerprints of fabrication.
